errors.text: The predicted fracture-strain trend is reversed: the target reports an increase from about 11.6% to 14.0%, whereas the generated hypothesis predicts decreased or stagnant fracture strain.
The mechanical-test condition is incorrectly specified as tensile loading rather than room-temperature compression.

The lattice-contraction mechanism is misinterpreted. The target treats contraction from about 3.392 Å to 3.325 Å as evidence of Cr-induced lattice distortion and solid-solution hardening, while the generated hypothesis claims contraction reduces mismatch and limits hardening.
The baseline comparison incorrectly states that the Cr-free alloy has higher fracture strain than the Cr-containing alloy.
The falsification rule would reject the hypothesis upon observing the actual target result—an increased fracture strain—despite crack-extension impedance being a required mechanism.
